title: Ioannes Tzetzes, Commentary (scholia) on Lycophron's Alexandra / Иоанн Цец, Комментарий к «Александре» Ликофрона
author: John Tzetzes (formerly attributed to his brother Isaac), with older scholia
size: Scheer vol. II (1908): lxiv + 398 pp. (est. ~150k words).
edition: Scheer 1881/1908 (Weidmann), PD. Leone 2002 (Congedo) for the old scholia and paraphrases.
ru_evidence: Ancientrome.ru Lycophron page has Surikov's Alexandra translation and Kaukhchishvili's article on Lycophron's scholiasts, but no translation of the commentary. Ru-wiki 'Иоанн Цец' lists none.
en_evidence: ToposText work 860 carries a ChatGPT-4 machine translation of Scheer, self-described as done 'with more speed than accuracy'. There is no scholarly English translation.
other_translations: No modern translation listed in Cuypers' Hellenistic Bibliography; only Canter's Latin edition of 1601.
value: The key to the most obscure Hellenistic poem and a huge mythographic thesaurus with lost authors. It complements Surikov's Russian Alexandra. Setting a vetted multi-model translation beside the raw ChatGPT draft would showcase Neoscholia's method.
ai_feasibility: Medium. Tzetzes' allusive Byzantine prose, polemics and dense quotations are hard. The existing machine draft offers a baseline for measurable gains from cross-model review.
pilot_unit: Tzetzes' prolegomena plus commentary on Alexandra 1–100; est. ~12k words.
